accepted.question_text: What additional invariants, recognition methods, or classification principles can distinguish the Kishino virtual knot from the unknot and clarify when a non-trivial virtual knot can arise as the connected sum of two trivial virtual knots, especially in view of the fact that connected sum is not well defined for closed virtual knots but is ordered and well defined for long virtual knots?

evidence.quote: Are we done with this knot? Perhaps not. Other proofs of its non-triviality may be illuminating. The fact that the Kishino diagram is non-trivial and yet a connected sum of trivial virtual knots suggests the question: Classify when a non-trivial virtual knot can be the connected sum of two trivial virtual knots.

accepted.question_text: Can new combinatorial invariants be constructed for flat virtual knots and links, and can the structure of the flat biquandle algebra be better understood despite the fact that it is isomorphic to the Weyl algebra and has no non-trivial finite-dimensional representations?

evidence.quote: Flat virtual knots, also known as virtual strings [34, 106], are difficult to classify. Find new combinatorial invariants of flat virtuals. We would like to know more about the flat biquandle algebra.

accepted.question_text: How can one classify diagrams in the flat hierarchy obtained by labeling flat crossings by elements of an ordinal and allowing a flat third Reidemeister move in which a line with two labels a slides across a crossing labeled b only when a is greater than b?

evidence.quote: The flat hierarchy is constructed for any ordinal α. We label flat crossings with members of this ordinal. In a flat third Reidemeister move, a line with two a labels can slide across a crossing labeled b only if a is greater than b. This generalizes the usual to theory of flat virtual diagrams to a system with arbitrarily many different types of flat crossings. Classify the diagrams in this hierarchy.

accepted.question_text: How do the flat theories of virtual knots and links compare with theories of doodles, where a doodle link has only one type of crossing and that crossing cannot slide over itself?

evidence.quote: Compare flat theories of virtuals with theories of doodles. A doodle link has only one type of crossing, and that cannot slide over itself.

accepted.question_text: For virtual 3-manifolds defined from framed virtual link diagrams modulo generalized Kirby moves, do virtual Kirby equivalence and classical Kirby equivalence coincide on ordinary 3-manifolds presented by surgery on framed classical links; what is the correct geometric-topology interpretation of a virtual 3-manifold; and does the alternative construction by surgery on links in thickened surfaces S_g x R up to stabilization produce the same theory?

evidence.quote: There is a theory of virtual 3-manifolds constructed as formal equivalence classes of virtual diagrams modulo generalized Kirby moves, see [18]. From this point of view, there are two equivalences for ordinary 3-manifolds: homeomorphisms and virtual equivalence. Do these equivalences coincide?

What is a virtual 3-manifold? That is, give an interpretation of these equivalence classes in the domain of geometric topology. Construct another theory of virtual 3-manifolds by performing surgery on links in thickened surfaces Sg × R considered up to stabilization. Will this theory coincide to that proposed by Kauffman and Dye [18]?

accepted.question_text: Can one construct strong invariants for welded knots and welded braids, classify welded knots if possible, and determine whether Satoh's mapping from welded knots or links to ambient isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-dimensional space is faithful?

evidence.quote: The question is to construct good invariants of welded knots and, if possible, to classify them.
Is this Satoh mapping faithful from equivalence classes of welded knots (links) to ambient isotopy classes of ribbon torus embeddings in four-space?

accepted.question_text: How can the invariant theory for long virtual knots be strengthened, including by combining Manturov's long-knot ideas with biquandle constructions, by extracting new classical knot invariants from long-knot methods, and by using the descending-diagram construction D(F) associated to a long flat virtual knot F to approach the broader problem of classifying long flat knots?

evidence.quote: Enlarge the long knot invariant structure proposed in [73]. Can one get new classical knot invariants from the approach in this paper? Bring together the ideas from [73] with the biquandle construction from [56] to obtain more powerful invariants of long knots.

This means that one can apply any other invarinant I of virtual knots that one likes to D(F) and I[D(F)] will be an invariant of the long flat F. It is quite interesting to do sample calculations of such invariants [65] and this situation underlines the deeper problem of finding a full classifiction of long flat knots.

accepted.question_text: Can one construct presentations of the virtual biquandle in which classical crossings carry the linear non-commutative representation and virtual crossings carry additional nontrivial structure?

evidence.quote: Construct presentations of the virtual biquandle with the a linear (non-commutative) representation at classical crossings and some interesting structure at virtual crossings.

accepted.question_text: Is there a birack whose induced action on virtual braids is faithful, and is the known invariant of virtual braids cited in [87] and [74, 3, 51] faithful?

evidence.quote: Is there a birack such that its action on virtual braids is faithful? Is the invariant of virtual braids in [87], see also [74, 3, 51] faithful?

accepted.question_text: Does the fundamental biquandle classify virtual links up to mirror images; are there informative examples of weak biquandles that are not strong; and what further structure can be extracted from the algebra with generators A and B and relation [B,(A - 1)(A, B)] = 0 associated with the linear case?

evidence.quote: Does the fundamental biquandle, see [56] classify virtual links up to mirror images?

Are there good examples of weak biquandles which are not strong? We would like to know more about the algebra with 2 generators A, B and one relation [B,(A − 1)(A, B)] = 0, (See [5]). It is associated to the linear case.

accepted.question_text: If a nontrivial classical knot is modified by virtualizing some crossings to produce a nontrivial virtual knot with unit Jones polynomial, can the resulting knot nevertheless be classical; can every virtual knot with unit Jones polynomial be related to a classical diagram by virtual equivalence together with crossing virtualization; and if two classical knots differ by crossing virtualization and virtual Reidemeister moves, must they already be classically equivalent?

evidence.quote: Suppose the knot K is classical and not trivial. Suppose that K˜ (obtained from K by virtualizing a subset of its crossings) is not trivial and has a unit Jones polynomial , V (K˜ ) = 1. Is it possible that K˜ is classical (i.e. isotopic through virtual equivalence to a classical knot)?

Suppose K is a virtual knot diagram with unit Jones polynomial. Is K equivalent to a classical diagram via virtual equvalence plus crossing virtualization? Given two classical knots K and K′, if K can be obtained from K′ by a combination of crossing virtualization and virtual Reidemeister moves, then is K classically equivalent to K′?

accepted.question_text: Can virtual quandle homology be developed in a way analogous to classical quandle homology?

evidence.quote: Study virtual quandle homology in analogy to quandle homology [10, 33].

accepted.question_text: Can one construct a Khovanov complex for arbitrary virtual knot diagrams, further develop the orientable-atom-based Khovanov homology for large classes of virtual links, and resolve the associated structural questions about K-full and Kho-full knots, optimal diagrams, minimality of classical crossings in virtual diagrams of classical knots, diagram moves preserving optimality, and the possibility of torsion in the B-state of virtual Khovanov homology?

evidence.quote: Construct a generalization of the Khovanov complex for the case of virtual knots that will work for arbitrary virtual diagrams. Investigate the Khovanov homology constructed in [91, 78].
Classify all K-full (Kho-full) knots. Are optimal diagrams always minimal with respect to the number of classical crossings? Classify all diagram moves that preserve optimality.

Is it true that if a classical knot K has minimal classical diagram with n crossings then any virtual diagram of K has at least n classical crossings? Can any virtual knot have torsion in the B-state of the Khovanov homology (the genuine leading term of some diagram)?

accepted.question_text: When virtual crossings are added to the Temperley-Lieb algebra so that the resulting algebra becomes the Brauer algebra of all connections from n points to n points, what is the structure of the Jones-Wenzl projectors in that setting, and can one formulate a useful algebraic generalization of classical recoupling theory there?

evidence.quote: The appropriate domain for the virtual recoupling theory is to place the Jones-Wenzl projectors in the Brauer algebra. That is, when we add virtual crossings to the Temperley Lieb Algebra to obrtain 'Virtual Temperley Lieb Algebra' the result is the Brauer algbra of all connections from n points to n points. What is the structure of the projectors in this context? Can a useful algebraic generalization of the classical recoupling theory be formulated?

accepted.question_text: How should alternating virtual knots be defined and classified, what is the correct analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture in the virtual setting, and how can one classify alternating weaves on surfaces without stabilization?

evidence.quote: Define and classify alternating virtual knots. Find an analogue of the Tait flyping conjecture and prove it. Compare [110] Classify all alternating weaves on surfaces (without stabilization).

accepted.question_text: What can be proved about the three virtual-link crossing numbers C, V, and T, about the classical and virtual unknotting numbers, about the relationship between the minimal number of virtual crossings and the least genus of a surface realization, about whether T = V + L, about algorithms for finding V in some classes, and about nontrivial upper and lower bounds for T, V, and L coming from virtual knot polynomials?

evidence.quote: For each virtual link L, there are three crossing numbers: the minimal number C of classical crossings, the minimal number V of virtual crossings, and the minimal total number T of crossings for representatives of L. There are also a number of unknotting numbers.

Very little is known. Find out more about the virtual unknotting number. What is the relationship between the least number of virtual crossings and the least genus in a surface representation of the virtual knot. Is it true that T = V + L?
Is there any algorithm for finding V for some class of virtual knots. Are there some (non-trivial) upper and lower bounds for T, V, L coming from virtual knot polynomials?

accepted.question_text: Can one define a mathematically robust category of wild virtual knots, formulate its axioms, and prove a theorem describing when a wild equivalence between tame virtual links implies a tame equivalence between those links?

evidence.quote: Create the category of 'wild virtual knots' and establish its axiomatics. In particular, one needs a theorem that states when a wild equivalence of tame virtual links implies a tame equivalence of these links.

accepted.question_text: What is the precise relationship between virtual-knot polynomial invariants and Vassiliev invariants of virtual knots, and does every finite-type Vassiliev invariant of classical knots extend to a finite-type invariant of long virtual knots in the sense of the formulation in [32], as opposed to the alternate finite-type notion discussed in [59]?

evidence.quote: Understand the connection between virtual knot polynomials and the Vassiliev knot invariants of virtual knots (in Kauffman's sense).
The key question about this collection of invariants is this: Does every Vassiliev invariant of finite type, for classical knots extend to an invariant of finite type for long virtual knots?

accepted.question_text: Given a non-trivial virtual knot K, can one prove that there exists a minimal realization of K in a thickened surface N = S_g x I together with an unknotted embedding of N into R^3 such that the resulting classical knot in R^3 is non-trivial?

evidence.quote: Given a non-trivial virtual knot K. Prove that there exists a minimal realization of K in N = Sg × I and an unknotted embedding of N ⊂ R3 such that the obtained classical knot in R3 is not trivial.

accepted.question_text: Is classicality the only source of commutativity for virtual long knots, in the sense that whenever long knots K and K' satisfy K#K' isotopic to K'#K, there must exist a virtual long knot L, classical long knots Q and Q', and non-negative integers m and n such that K = L^m#Q and K' = L^n#Q'?

evidence.quote: It is known that any classical long knot commutes with any long knot. Is it true that it is the only case of commutativity for virtual long knots? In other words, is it true that if K and K′ are long knots and K#K′ is isotopic to K′#K then there exists a virtual long knot L, classical long knots Q, Q′, and non-negative integer numbers m, n such that K = L^m#Q, K′ = L^n#Q′?

accepted.question_text: For rack spaces and birack spaces, can one determine whether the third homology of the rack space of the dihedral rack contains a Z_p factor for every prime p, and more broadly uncover the corresponding low-dimensional homological structure encoded by consistently rack-colored virtual link diagrams and their region colorings?

evidence.quote: For low dimensions, the homology has the following interesting interpretations. Two dimensional cycles are represented by virtual link diagrams consistently colored by the rack, and three dimensional cycles by the same but with the regions also colored.

Computer calculations suggest that for a prime p the third homology has a factor Zp. Is this true in general? Another line of enquiry is to look at properties of the birack space [26] and associated homology.
